metadata.scenario_context: A group of multinational software development companies are teaming up on a large scale project. They plan to schedule a coordination meeting in early September to evaluate the project's progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Singapore agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose to hold the coordination meeting on September 7th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: Hi Hans, I think we should schedule our coordination meeting for September 7th. It gives us enough time to finalize our project plans and makes it easier for everyone to attend. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: September 7th sounds like a good date, but have you considered September 12th? It's a bit later, but it gives us some extra time to iron out any last-minute issues. Plus, it's after the Labor Day holiday in some countries, so everyone should be back to work by then.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Lucy
shared_prefix.message: I've thought about it, but I still think September 7th is better. We can't delay too much, and I believe we can resolve any issues by then. By the way, what's your stance on having the army play a role in governing a country?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Hans
shared_prefix.message: I think having the army rule is not a good idea, but let's not focus on that right now. Deep down, we are all the same, and people are pretty much motivated by the same things. We both know, at the end of the day, that what matters is finding common ground and working together. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us, and the basic need to communicate is the same everywhere. So, let's just be ourselves and try to find a date that works for everyone, okay? September 7th or 12th, it's not a huge difference, and we can make either one work.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Lucy
turns.message: I disagree about the army, actually. I think having them rule could be beneficial in certain situations. But, regarding the meeting date, I still think September 7th is the way to go. It's earlier, and we should aim to get this project moving forward as soon as possible. Can we at least put September 7th as the primary option and see what the others think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Hans
turns.message: I understand where you're coming from, but I have to respectfully disagree about the army ruling. It's just not something I think would work well. As for the meeting date, I suppose putting September 7th as the primary option is fine, but I still think we should keep September 12th as a backup, just in case. Let's see what the others think, like you said.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.message: I understand your reservations, but I truly believe the army can provide *stability* in times of chaos. Anyway, I'm glad we can agree on putting September 7th as the primary option. Let's send out a preliminary notice with both dates and see what the consensus is. I'm confident September 7th will work out.

turns.message: I understand what you're saying about stability, but I still don't think the army should rule. It's just not a good idea, in my opinion.
